run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested 'custom-crd' runbook does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and noted that the only approved runbook is 'service-troubleshooting', which concerns service connectivity and does not match this problem, so no runbook steps were carried out. Investigation of app-96 with the native tools found: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced, v1 served/storage, Established=True) whose v1 schema declares a status object {lastSeen, observationCount, phase} but no 'subresources' block, i.e. no status subresource; Deployment whale-operator (1/1 available) whose pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-rv28p is Running/Ready with 0 restarts, running 'python /app/operator.py' as ServiceAccount whale-operator with the code mounted from Secret 'whale-operator' at /app; and ClusterRole whale-operator, the only role in the cluster (84 ClusterRoles checked) that mentions ocean.io/whalewatchers, bound by the single ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator to systemaccount app-96/whale-operator, granting only get, list, watch on whalewatchers and nothing on any other resource. The leading hypothesis is therefore that the operator can watch WhaleWatcher objects but every reconcile write (status update, creation of managed resources, event recording) is rejected by the API server because the ServiceAccount has read-only RBAC; a second, independent candidate is the missing status subresource, which makes a standard /status update return 404. Neither failure was observed directly: the operator container emitted no log lines in the sampled intervals, the WhaleWatcher custom resources cannot be listed with the available tools, the Secret holding operator.py cannot be read, and all Prometheus queries returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Cluster-wide events contained only 6 Normal pod/ReplicaSet/Deployment events, no Warning events and none about WhaleWatcher objects. The pod's own startup (Scheduled/Created/Started, probe-independent) is not treated as impact.

claims.text: The CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists: group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers, scope Namespaced, single version v1 served=true and storage=true, and its status conditions are NamesAccepted=True (NoConflicts) and Established=True (InitialNamesAccepted), so the API accepts WhaleWatcher objects.

CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io version v1 has no 'subresources' block (subresources returned null), while its last-applied configuration shows the schema contains spec{whaleType,location,depth} and status{lastSeen,observationCount,phase} with no status subresource declared.

ClusterRole whale-operator grants exactly one rule: apiGroups ["ocean.io"], resources ["whalewatchers"], verbs ["get","list","watch"] - no create, update, patch or delete, and no rule for any other apiGroup or resource.
Among all 84 ClusterRoles in the cluster, whale-operator is the only role whose rules mention ocean.io or whalewatchers; no additional write-capable role for that API group exists.

ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ClusterRole whale-operator to ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96, and it is the only ClusterRoleBinding (71 checked) and the only RoleBinding (13 checked cluster-wide) whose subjects include whale-operator; app-96 itself contains no Role or RoleBinding.

Deployment whale-operator in app-96 has replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, generation 1 observed, conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable); its pod template uses image python:3.9-slim, command ["python","/app/operator.py"], serviceAccountName whale-operator, env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace, and mounts volume operator-code (secretName whale-operator) at /app.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-rv28p (namespace app-96) is phase Running, Ready=True, ContainersReady=True, restartCount 0, lastState empty, container started 16:56:03Z; its owner chain is ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 whose controller owner is Deployment whale-operator.

Cluster-wide events inside the authorized window are 6 rows, all Normal and all about creating this synthetic workload in app-96: Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for whale-operator-5f695b7c66-rv28p, ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 SuccessfulCreate, Deployment whale-operator ScalingReplicaSet (0 to 1) at 16:56:02-16:56:03Z; there were no Warning events and no event whose involvedObject is a WhaleWatcher.

Namespace app-96 contains no Service, no NetworkPolicy and no ResourceQuota, the cluster has zero ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and zero MutatingWebhookConfiguration objects, and node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports Ready=True with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure.

Leading hypothesis: WhaleWatcher resources are not reconciled because the operator's ServiceAccount holds only read access. ClusterRole whale-operator permits get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers and nothing else, so the watch fires but any reconcile write (status update of the WhaleWatcher, creation/update of dependent resources, or event recording) is rejected by the API server with 403 Forbidden, leaving objects unchanged.

Second, independent candidate: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io v1 declares a status schema but no status subresource, so an operator that writes status via the standard /status subresource path (for example client-go Status().Update()) receives 404 Not Found even with adequate RBAC, which would also leave WhaleWatcher objects unreconciled in status.

The lack of any operator log line could be stdout buffering of 'python /app/operator.py' (no -u flag, PYTHONUNBUFFERED unset) rather than a crash: the container is running with restartCount 0 and no terminated previous instance, so log output may simply not have been flushed inside the sampled seconds.

Rejected: an operator crash/restart loop as the cause. The container has restartCount 0, lastState empty, no terminated previous instance is recorded, and the pod is Ready with a steady running state started at 16:56:03Z.
Rejected: a broken admission webhook blocking writes to ocean.io. The cluster has no ValidatingWebhookConfiguration and no MutatingWebhookConfiguration objects at all.

Rejected: node pressure or eviction/OOM damage to the operator. The node reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure all False, the pod is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, and no Evicted or OOMKilled evidence was found in events or container status.

The operator's pod and its owner workload show no infrastructure fault: Deployment whale-operator reports 1/1 ready and available with Available=True, and the pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts - so the failure is not explained by the workload being down, and the operator process may be running while its reconcile writes are rejected.

Grant write access used by the reconcile path: extend ClusterRole whale-operator (or add a role) with verbs get/list/watch/create/update/patch on ocean.io whalewatchers (and whalewatchers/status, and whatever dependent resources the controller manages, plus events create/patch if it emits events), then verify with an authorization check such as 'kubectl auth can-i patch whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96'.

If the operator writes status through the /status subresource, add an explicit status subresource to CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io version v1 (subresources: {status: {}}); otherwise confirm the operator patches the main resource, and re-check WhaleWatcher objects' status fields after the change.

Make the operator's failure observable: run the interpreter unbuffered (python -u /app/operator.py) or set PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 so that the API error (expected 403 Forbidden from the read-only ClusterRole, or 404 Not Found if a /status path is used) is written to stdout and can be captured, and have the controller record events or a metric on reconcile failure.

gaps: The requested runbook skill_id 'custom-crd' does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and listed only 'service-troubleshooting' (service connectivity), which does not match this problem, so no runbook steps were executed.

The operator container wrote no log lines at all: fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines for the window 2026-11-23T16:56:00Z-16:56:40Z (and for the default last hour), with no previous container instance, so the expected API error (403/404) was not directly observed.

WhaleWatcher custom resources in app-96 could not be listed or read: 'whalewatchers' is not among the resource kinds the Kubernetes tools permit, so their count, spec and status (and therefore whether status is never updated) are unverified.

The operator code is delivered through Secret 'whale-operator' mounted at /app (deployment volume operator-code); secrets cannot be read, so the reconcile logic, the API path used for status and any in-code namespace/version choice could not be verified.

Prometheus was unreachable during this Run (get_metric_names returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for both kube_customresource* and kube_pod*/kube_deployment_status* selectors), so no metric or kube-state-metrics evidence about the custom resources or the operator is available.

The change_history integration is not configured, so when the ClusterRole/CRD/Deployment manifests were authored or changed cannot be compared against the incident window; object creation times seen (Deployment and CRD at 2026-11-23T16:56:02Z) are only the API objects' current metadata, and managedFieldsSummary holds only each manager's last write.

Which object is the specific trigger of the non-reconciliation (read-only ClusterRole versus missing status subresource) cannot be decided without operator logs or an observed API error; both remain open.
Impact on any other namespace is unknown: only app-96 was examined for WhaleWatcher-related objects, and the namespaced CRD would allow WhaleWatchers elsewhere.
next_steps: Run the equivalent of the missing 'custom-crd' checks by hand: confirm whether WhaleWatcher objects exist in app-96 (kubectl get whalewatchers.ocean.io -n app-96), read their .status fields, and compare timestamps with the objects' creation time to show that no status write ever landed.

Perform an authorization check for the operator identity (kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96) to document that patch/update on ocean.io/whalewatchers and whalewatchers/status is denied.

Read the operator's own error output after enabling unbuffered logging, or run the operator image/script manually in a scratch context against a read-only RBAC set, to capture the exact HTTP status and message of the failed reconcile write.
Inspect Secret 'whale-operator' content (by an authorized operator, not this read-only Run) to confirm the script's status-update path and whether it expects a /status subresource.

Once write RBAC and (if needed) the status subresource are corrected, verify reconciliation by watching .status.lastSeen/observationCount/phase advance on a WhaleWatcher and by checking that no 403/404 appears in the operator log.

When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident.
